authority: CEO Round 132 deep audit — 'Stop calling Python B/C independent external solver worlds. The previous G18=GREEN must be revoked.'
preamble: This document formally revokes the Round 131 claim of '5 genuinely independent solver worlds.' The correct classification is 3 external solver/package worlds + 2 custom in-repository Python formulations. G18 is downgraded from GREEN to PARTIAL_INSUFFICIENT_FOR_PROMOTION.

WORLD_A_FEBIO.note: Genuinely external solver. Compiled from official FEBio source. Different organization, different codebase, different developers from all other worlds.

WORLD_B_CUSTOM_PERIDYNAMIC_FORMULATION.independence_grade: PARTIAL — provides mathematical model-form diversity but NOT external solver evidence
WORLD_B_CUSTOM_PERIDYNAMIC_FORMULATION.limitation: Authored inside the discovery repository by the same coder. Implements peridynamic theory but is NOT the Peridigm binary. Cannot substitute for actual Peridigm execution.
WORLD_B_CUSTOM_PERIDYNAMIC_FORMULATION.what_it_provides: Mathematical formulation diversity (nonlocal bond-based vs FEM+CDM vs finite-volume vs elastic-plastic vs linear-elastic).
WORLD_B_CUSTOM_PERIDYNAMIC_FORMULATION.what_it_does_NOT_provide: External evidence-source independence. The code was written by the same person who wrote the other worlds. It could share hidden assumptions with the other custom world.

WORLD_C_CUSTOM_FLOW_FORMULATION.independence_grade: PARTIAL — provides mathematical model-form diversity but NOT external solver evidence
WORLD_C_CUSTOM_FLOW_FORMULATION.limitation: Authored inside the discovery repository by the same coder. Implements flow+erosion physics but is NOT the clotFoam binary. Cannot substitute for actual clotFoam execution.
WORLD_C_CUSTOM_FLOW_FORMULATION.critical_note: This is the ONLY world where C5's precursor was detected. The positive result exists ONLY in a custom in-repository implementation. This must be treated as a potential artifact, not a confirmed discovery.
WORLD_C_CUSTOM_FLOW_FORMULATION.what_it_provides: Mathematical formulation diversity (flow-driven vs mechanical failure).
WORLD_C_CUSTOM_FLOW_FORMULATION.what_it_does_NOT_provide: External evidence-source independence. The C5 positive result in this world is suspect until reproduced in actual clotFoam.

WORLD_D_CALCULIX.source: C from Guido Dhondt (github.com/CalculiX), installed via conda-forge
WORLD_D_CALCULIX.note: Genuinely external solver. Different codebase (C vs FEBio's C++), different developer (Dhondt vs University of Utah), different element formulations.

WORLD_E_SFEPY.note: Genuinely external package. Different codebase, different developers, different element technology from FEBio and CalculiX.

G18_correction.rationale: G18 requires ALL worlds to be externally independent for promotion-grade credit. 3 of 5 worlds (FEBio, CalculiX, SfePy) are genuinely external. 2 of 5 (custom peridynamics, custom flow) are in-repository Python models authored by the same coder. Formulation diversity ≠ evidence-source independence. Per CEO Round 132: 'You cannot make G18 GREEN simply because source code A ≠ source code B. The question is: How much independent epistemic ancestry does World B have from World A?'
G18_correction.promotion_implication: G18 = PARTIAL means NO candidate can be promoted to WORLD_CLASS_INVENTION until Worlds B and C are replaced with actual Peridigm and clotFoam binaries, OR until the custom formulations are independently validated against published benchmarks from the external solvers.

distinction_introduced.FORMULATION_DIVERSITY: Different mathematical formulations (FEM, peridynamics, finite-volume, elastic-plastic, linear-elastic). This is ACHIEVED.
distinction_introduced.EVIDENCE_SOURCE_INDEPENDENCE: Different organizations, different codebases, different developers, different maintenance histories. This is PARTIALLY achieved (3 of 5).
